chunks: And from him, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Uthafir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about my joining with someone whom I follow in prayer, reading behind him in the second rak'ah, so he bows when I finish reciting the Mother of the Book. He said: 'Recite in the last two [rak'ahs] so that you have recited in two rak'ahs.'
ai.seo_question: What should a follower do if they finish reciting Al-Fatiha before the Imam bows in the second rak'ah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential ruling for followers who recite Surah Al-Fatiha independently behind the Imam, specifically addressing the timing of their completion relative to the Imam's bowing. It establishes that to ensure the validity of their individual recitation obligation, they must continue reciting in the subsequent rak'ahs rather than remaining silent, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the follower's active participation in the prayer's pillars. This highlights the scholarly distinction between mere following (mutaba'ah) and the fulfillment of personal obligatory acts (fara'id) within the congregational setting.
